analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview Feedback Across the Board
key_insights: Gas infrastructure is one of the most topical groups on the GS desk over the last 72 hours. Generalist interest has grown over two years, and focus has shifted from E&Ps into Midstream.

KMI reported a very strong set of results on Wednesday after the close. The backlog step-up was well above buyside and sellside expectations (more buyside inbounds had expected a $1-$2bn increase). The follow-up question from investors is what to do with the stock now.

Positioning into KMI earnings was tilted more positive than in several quarters (desk read 7/10), and some investors are asking whether defending the position is the next step despite the strong update.

WMB screens as well owned into EPS and has been one of the more well owned stocks over the last year plus. Investor focus is on the BTM project execution path and contract announcement. GS is running scenarios (small project, no project, no project plus Transco updates). Feedback is that even a quiet quarter should be fine.
Before yesterday, little or no power value was embedded in LBRT, KGS and PUMP. After yesterday, valuations are nearly fully back to base business levels.

LBRT's EPS was the most topical print. The 500 MW headline eased concerns that it could be two contracts, an industrial player or a non-AI customer. The contract remains TBD and there are still financing questions.
Across the power spectrum (BTM, IPPs, solar, battery storage, regulated utilities, nuclear), BTM still screens as the pocket of the market more investors are excited about.
Refining: specialists are searching for reasons to buy the 3Q prints. VLO printed $23.90 of EPS in the quarter while the buyside was looking for closer to $25.

VLO is sitting on $10bn of cash. Buybacks will continue, and feedback has been constructive on building cash at these levels. The market looks to VLO as an indicator of how refiners will position balance sheets for a return to mid-cycle cracks.

Cracks have rolled over recently. With stocks still near highs, 4Q revisions in focus, high bars into EPS and cash balances scrutinized, more specialists are leaning cautious on the near-term setup for refining.

sector_views.rationale: More specialists are leaning cautious on the near-term setup because cracks have rolled, stocks are near highs, 4Q revisions are in focus and the bar into EPS is high.
Continued investor interest in gas pipes. Focus has moved from E&Ps to Midstream, and KMI's backlog step-up was well above expectations.
